**Visa and Lianlian complete China's first B2B agentic transaction**

*Cross-border B2B agentic payments raise unresolved questions about authentication, liability and compliance standards that consumer-focused European pilots have not yet had to address.*

Visa and Lianlian DigiTech have completed what they describe as the first live business-to-business agentic transaction in China, using Lianlian's LoopXPay AI agent. The transaction was processed through Visa's network, with an AI agent initiating and completing a cross-border payment on behalf of a business customer.

The development extends the agentic payments trend that has been gathering pace in Europe. ING, Worldline and Mastercard completed Europe's first agentic payment in June, Crédit Agricole followed with a production transaction shortly after, and Visa itself ran agentic payments in Europe the same month. Agentic commerce has now crossed into B2B and into a market where AI-native payment infrastructure is developing rapidly.

B2B agentic payments will likely require new standards for authentication, liability and dispute resolution that go beyond what current consumer-focused pilots have tested. Cross-border B2B adds complexity around sanctions screening, trade compliance and multi-currency settlement that consumer-facing agentic transactions do not encounter.

*Sources: [Visa and Lianlian enable China's first B2B agentic transaction](https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/110488/visa-and-lianlian-enable-chinas-first-b2b-agentic-transaction?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

**Mastercard broadens virtual card platform for B2B payments**

*Enhancements to Mastercard's In Control platform reflect continued investment in virtual card infrastructure as card networks defend B2B territory against account-to-account alternatives.*

Mastercard has announced a series of enhancements to its In Control virtual card number platform, expanding functionality for corporate buyers and their suppliers. The updates are designed to make virtual cards more scalable for B2B payment flows.

Account-to-account competition in B2B payments is intensifying. NMI's acquisition of Dwolla, PaidBy's partnership with Mastercard itself on cross-border account-to-account payments, and the broader push toward instant payment rails for business transactions all represent alternatives to card-based B2B settlement. Mastercard's response is to deepen the virtual card proposition rather than cede the segment.

Virtual cards have gained traction in corporate travel, procurement and accounts payable because they offer controls, data and reconciliation advantages over traditional invoicing. The platform investment suggests Mastercard treats B2B virtual cards as a durable revenue line, not a transitional product.

*Sources: [Mastercard expands virtual card programme](https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/110490/mastercard-expands-virtual-card-programme?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*
